_comment: P94 claim-proof binding (drift invariant 60, tools/sync_check.py::check_claim_proof). A universal claim about this repo's own behavior is a promise, and a promise ships with the executed proof that keeps it. `claims` bind a verbatim sentence to either an enforced drift invariant (`invariant:N`) or a NAMED selftest pin the battery actually runs (`tools/x.py::selftest::<label substring>`). `exempt` records a universal that no code can prove -- a standing instruction to the agent -- with a written reason. `routes` bind an install route the docs RECOMMEND to the code that must DETECT it. `corpus` is the guarded set: a universal claim there that appears in none of the three lists fails the build.
_why: Documentation truth checks paths, symbols, counts, URLs and hashes, and a universal sentence names none of those, so no token check can see it; this manifest ties each such sentence to an executed proof or a written exemption.

claims.claim: No em dashes in user-facing output
claims.proof: invariant:4
claims.why: invariant 4 (check_formatting) proves the no-em-dash rule over committed examples/ content, which is the scope the same bullet states; the wider instruction to the agent is covered by the formatting protocol it cites.

claims.claim: runs with no model tokens: outside its selftests, the code it runs imports only the standard library plus `registry_io` and `atomic_io`, starts no process, sends requests only to `pypi.org` and `api.github.com`, and reads one credential from the environment, a GitHub token
claims.proof: tools/dependency_currency.py::selftest::token-free: outside its selftests the import closure
claims.why: The selftest reads the import closure of dependency_currency.py statically, skipping the functions named selftest and _selftest. It fails on a module outside the standard library other than registry_io and atomic_io, on a refused standard-library module (subprocess, multiprocessing, concurrent, importlib, runpy, ctypes, pty, webbrowser, asyncio, pkgutil, zipimport, builtins, code, codeop, pickle, marshal, shelve, _posixsubprocess, socket, socketserver, http, ftplib, smtplib, imaplib, poplib, nntplib, telnetlib, xmlrpc), on a process-spawning or dynamic-code call, on a network call outside _http_get_json, on an environment read other than REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, GITHUB_TOKEN or GH_TOKEN, and when _ALLOWED_HOSTS is anything but pypi.org and api.github.com. It also hands _http_get_json a recording opener: a URL on another host is refused before anything is sent, and a redirect to another host is refused. It reads code, not traffic: a credential read from a file is not seen. A model request needs a model host, which the host check refuses, or a process or model client, which the closure check refuses; the conclusion rests on pypi.org and api.github.com serving no model inference.

claims.claim: drift invariant 19 refuses tracked personal `*.local.*` files
claims.proof: invariant:19
claims.why: check_local_privacy fails when git ls-files lists a file whose basename matches the personal *.local.* pattern (fail-closed in CI when git is unavailable).

claims.claim: Every spoke in the hub's downstream list exists;
claims.proof: invariant:6
claims.why: check_hub parses the fenced list under the hub's "## Downstream spokes" heading and fails on a listed name with no skills/<name>/ directory, and on a spoke directory the list omits; a fixture self-proof of both directions runs first.

claims.claim: Every registry entry carries a `default_flag` naming one of the registry's declared `states`; drift invariant 53 checks that and runs the resolver and its `--list` and `--plan` output over the committed registry, so a missing or undeclared default, or an entry the resolver or its CLI cannot process, fails the build.
claims.proof: invariant:53
claims.why: check_connector_resolver_smoke refuses any committed default_flag that is not a bare string from connectors.json's own `states` list (a self-proof on misspelled, boolean, numeric, empty, missing and dict values runs first), then executes resolve({}) and connectors.py --list, --plan and --plan --json over the committed registry and fails on any exception (a self-proof with a raising registry loader proves all three CLI paths run).

claims.claim: the code side never writes into a machine-wide site-packages at all
claims.proof: tools/setup.py::selftest::pip census: every pip install command in the tree is built in
claims.why: the census parses every .py file in the tree (hidden, build and cache directories excluded) and fails unless the only pip install argv literals sit in setup.py::_pip_install and wizard.py::_install_uv; the install-target pins in the setup.py and wizard.py selftests then record the interpreter each of those two runs pip with.

claims.claim: Drift invariant 59 enforces the labeling across every tracked guidance file
claims.proof: invariant:59
claims.why: check_install_scope derives its denominator from git ls-files, so 'every tracked guidance file' is the scanned set rather than a hand list.

claims.claim: is gated behind the `live_publishing_enabled` flag (default off)
claims.proof: tools/publishing_compliance.py::selftest::the committed creator-os-config.json ships live_publishing_enabled off
claims.why: the named pin reads the committed creator-os-config.json (never the gitignored local override) and asserts the master flag is off there; its sibling pin asserts an unset flag reads as off.

claims.proof: tools/setup.py::selftest::pip census: every pip install command in the tree is built in
claims.why: the same pip census as the CLAUDE.md non-negotiable; this is the policy page's statement of it.

claims.claim: Every remaining `brew install`
claims.proof: invariant:59
claims.why: the completeness half of this sentence is exactly what check_install_scope proves over the derived denominator; it was false when the denominator was a 16-file list.

claims.claim: The drift guard enforces this for `examples/` only.
claims.proof: invariant:4
claims.why: this sentence states the enforced scope exactly, and check_formatting is what enforces it.

claims.claim:
nothing under `/Applications`,
  `/opt/homebrew`, or via `sudo` unless explicitly labeled
claims.proof: invariant:59
claims.why: check_install_scope scans every tracked guidance file for exactly these machine-wide forms and fails on any that is unlabeled.

claims.claim: **Human confirmation required before every post.**
claims.proof: tools/dashboard/server.py::selftest::every flag on: a post no human confirmed never reaches the network
claims.why: the dashboard selftest sends forged confirmation fields through the add, import, caption, toggle and schedule endpoints, then runs the real scheduler loop with every publishing flag on while recording at urllib.request.urlopen and socket.create_connection, and observes zero calls. Sibling pins show Confirm does mark the post scheduled and dispatch() refuses an entry not passed confirmed=True.

claims.claim:
Nothing goes to `/Applications`, `/opt/homebrew`,
`/usr/local`, or anywhere `sudo` is needed.
claims.proof: invariant:59
claims.why: the same derived-denominator scan proves no unlabeled instruction to install in those locations survives in the guidance.

claims.claim: The `schedule_post` MCP tool (`tools/mcp_server.py`) always sets `human_review_required: true`
claims.proof: tools/mcp_server.py::selftest::schedule_post always sets human_review_required: true on every platform and tier
claims.why: _selftest_static runs _schedule_post_impl, the whole body of the MCP tool, for all four platforms on the manual, direct_api-without-credentials and direct_api-with-token tiers and asserts the flag on all twelve summaries; a structural pin asserts the tool returns that summary unchanged.

claims.claim: the repo `.venv` is the only install target
claims.proof: tools/setup.py::selftest::.venv present: every pip and Playwright subprocess runs the .venv interpreter
claims.why: install_dependencies runs with env_paths reporting a .venv path and the module's subprocess swapped for an argv recorder while ensure_venv, _pip_install and _install_playwright_browser stay real; every recorded argv[0] must be that path, so a fallback to the base interpreter in install_dependencies or inside _pip_install fails the pin.

claims.why: with env_paths finding no .venv and ensure_venv left real, install_dependencies starts only the `python -m venv` creation attempt (recorded at the subprocess argv, not run) and no pip or Playwright call, so nothing falls back to the base interpreter; a sibling pin checks every requirements set is refused with the remedy text.

claims.claim: advances items to `ready_to_post` for manual posting and makes no network call
claims.proof: tools/dashboard/server.py::selftest::scheduler flag off: every due item advances to ready_to_post and no network call is made
claims.why: the dashboard selftest runs the real _scheduler_loop for one pass with the master flag off (with no flags set, and with every platform flag on), records at urllib.request.urlopen and socket.create_connection, and observes zero calls with every due item at ready_to_post; a flag-on control proves the recorder sees the upload attempt, and dispatch() independently refuses when the flag it reads is off.

claims.claim: `tools/wizard.py::_install_uv`)
claims.proof: tools/wizard.py::selftest::no .venv: _install_uv refuses and starts no subprocess
claims.why: names the wizard's own uv install as the second code path; its selftest pin runs _install_uv with no .venv and requires a refusal and zero subprocess calls, and a sibling pin requires the one pip call to use the .venv interpreter when a .venv exists.

claims.proof: tools/wizard.py::selftest::.venv present: _install_uv runs pip only with the .venv interpreter
claims.why: the wizard selftest runs _install_uv with a .venv present and requires exactly one subprocess call, a pip install whose argv[0] is the .venv interpreter; a sibling pin covers the no-.venv refusal.

claims.claim: invariant 20 refuses tracked `pipeline/` files beyond the blank templates and tracked data-file types
claims.proof: invariant:20
claims.why: check_pipeline_allowlist fails on a tracked pipeline/ file outside PIPELINE_TRACKED_ALLOWLIST and on any tracked file whose suffix is in secret_scan.FORBIDDEN_DATA_SUFFIXES.

claims.claim: invariant 21 scans tracked content for known secret formats, non-allowlisted email addresses
claims.proof: invariant:21
claims.why: check_secret_content runs tools/secret_scan.py --tracked over every tracked text file: PATTERNS cover API keys, private keys, credential values, session links and non-allowlisted emails, and AMOUNT_RE covers dollar figures under pipeline/.

claims.claim: North American phone numbers whose digit groups are split by a dash, dot, single space or area-code parenthesis
claims.proof: tools/secret_scan.py::selftest::phone number detected in the paren, +1, 1-prefix, dotted and extension NANP shapes
claims.why: the secret_scan selftest builds paren, +1, 1-prefix, dotted and extension fixtures by concatenation and requires a phone_number finding for each while dates, versions, ISBNs and ports stay clean; invariant 21 runs the same PATTERNS over tracked content. A single digit run, a slash-separated number and a spaced-dash number are not matched; the next sentence says so and a sibling selftest check pins it.

exempt.claim: Never fabricate data, metrics, rates, brands, or sources
exempt.why: A standing instruction to the agent about generated output, not a property of this repo's code. protocols/no-fabrication.md governs it and no guard can prove a negative about future generations.

exempt.claim: Nothing is released until it passes the Quality Gates
exempt.why: A release-process directive routed through the quality-review skill; there is no code path a drift invariant can execute to prove a human followed it.

exempt.claim: Installs are user-scoped by default: everything lands under the user's home folder
exempt.why: The policy statement whose provable halves are bound separately: invariant 59 for the guidance labeling, and for the code side the pip census and install-target pins in the tools/setup.py and tools/wizard.py selftests, which record the interpreter each pip subprocess runs in. This opening sentence summarises those bindings.

exempt.claim: Agents never post directly
exempt.why: a behavioral directive about how agents act; no guard can execute the negative. Its code-side boundary is bound through the bold headline of the same bullet, whose pin sends forged confirmation fields through the dashboard's add, import, caption, toggle and schedule-edit endpoints and observes no network call.

exempt.claim: Those two fields are the only baselines it reads
exempt.why: Describes dependency_currency's read surface, which invariant 25 constrains only at the requirements-versus-registry pin level; the read-surface half is maintainer documentation of the tool's design.

exempt.claim: Everything Creator OS asks a person to download or install lands inside their own user
exempt.why: The policy's opening statement of intent; its enforceable halves are bound separately, to invariant 59 for the guidance and to the pip census and install-target pins in the tools/setup.py and tools/wizard.py selftests for the code.

exempt.claim: wizard state, staged bundles, `dist/` builds -- all gitignored
exempt.why: A table row about gitignore coverage, which drift invariant 19 enforces for tracked .local. files; the row itself is descriptive.

exempt.claim: none needed -- the repository is public
exempt.why: A statement about GitHub repository visibility, a property of the remote that no local guard in this repo can assert.

exempt.claim: is written only through `tools/registry_io.py`
exempt.why: invariant 42 counts the sanctioned registry writers but is labelled advisory in its own docstring and does not gate the build on a new writer, so this is a maintainer convention backed by an advisory census rather than a proven property.

exempt.claim: is the only tool that writes to `traversal-candidates.json`
exempt.why: no guard inspects traversal-candidates.json or traversal-visited.json at all; this is a maintainer convention with no executed proof behind it, recorded here honestly rather than bound to a check that does not cover it.

exempt.claim: A universal claim ("no", "never", "every", "everything", "all", "each", "only", "nothing", "always", "none", "nobody", "cannot", "will not") in a
exempt.why: this sentence QUOTES the trigger vocabulary the rule governs; the words are the subject of the sentence rather than a promise being made.

exempt.claim: Write ranges with "to" everywhere, including internal docs
exempt.why: A writing instruction to the agent. Invariant 4 fails the build on an en dash in .md files under shared/, protocols/, skills/, docs/, examples/ and canonical-sources/; a hyphen range, and any file outside those folders, is unchecked, so 'everywhere' is doctrine rather than a checked property.

exempt.why: scopes which lane needs Node at all; the detectability obligation for that route is bound as a route record instead.

exempt.claim: works on every platform, fully user-scoped
exempt.why: describes faster-whisper's own portability, a property of that third-party package rather than of this repo's code.

exempt.claim: auth only if a machine must PUSH
exempt.why: states when GitHub credentials are needed, a fact about GitHub's access model that no local guard can assert.

it queries PyPI and GitHub Releases directly (stdlib, honoring the env proxy + CA bundle) and
  computes drift from each registry entry's own `validated_version` and `pinned_constraint`

exempt.claim:
No connector call is made, and no post is queued or published,
  without an explicit human confirmation step
exempt.why: restates the bold headline in negative form. Its code half is bound through that headline's dashboard pin (a post no human confirmed never reaches the network with every flag on); 'no connector call' also covers read connectors an agent might call, which is an agent directive no code can execute.

exempt.claim:
they produce

exempt.why: a behavioral directive about what agents produce, enforced by the confirmation step rather than by a guard that can execute the negative.

exempt.claim:
Machine-wide installation is always a labeled

exempt.why: the policy's statement of intent; the enforceable half (that no unlabeled machine-wide instruction survives) is bound to invariant 59 in the following sentence.

exempt.claim: written by the apps/tools themselves, always per-user
exempt.why: a table row describing where third-party apps place their own per-user config and caches; this repo neither writes nor controls those locations.

exempt.claim: `report`/`check` are read-only
exempt.why: describes the currency checker's two read-only verbs for maintainers; no guard asserts a CLI verb writes nothing.

exempt.claim:
a new
  guard's scan set is derived from the tree, never a hand list of the files the change happened
  to touch
exempt.why: a process precondition for writing a guard, checked by the reviewer at design time; no build step can tell whether a denominator was derived or recalled.

exempt.claim:
When a
  check fails, report it honestly with the output; never claim a skipped step ran.
exempt.why: an instruction governing what the agent says in a report; nothing in the build can read a chat message, so this is doctrine enforced by judgment.

routes.why: uv installs itself and `uv python install`'s pythonX.Y into ~/.local/bin (uv docs, Installing Python). P93 recommended this route while env_paths searched only the Homebrew prefixes and the launcher probed only machine-wide paths, so the Python its own message told the user to install was invisible.

nvm keeps each node under $NVM_DIR/versions/node/<version>/bin (nvm.sh::nvm_version_path) and is sourced per shell. P93 made nvm the recommended Node route while env_paths could not see it, so the wizard looped users on 'Still not detecting Node.js 20 or higher' after issuing its own nvm command.

_detector_branches_why: Recorded branch names for the two detectors that scan text. Fixture/branch agreement alone only catches a half delete; with the names recorded here, removing a branch AND its fixture in one edit still fails the build. A missing table, a missing key, or an entry that is not a non-empty list of names fails the check instead of skipping the pin.
